2026-10-30 Release 6.9.0¶

(last merged pull request is #3210)

This is an enhancement and bug fix release.

API Changes

  • Add support for Python 3.15 and drop support for Python 3.12 [#3200 and #3201 by Martin Holmer]

  • Remove FairShare tax parameters and variable [#3199 by Martin Holmer]

  • Remove AGI surtax parameters, code, tests, and documentation [#3202 by Martin Holmer]

  • Remove DependentCare function and associated parameters and variable [#3204 by Martin Holmer]

  • Remove ALD_InvInc_ec_base function and associated parameter and variable [#3205 by Martin Holmer]

New Features

  • Add make valtest command to agent instructions [#3189 by Martin Holmer]

  • Revise taxcalc/validation/pe_taxsim documentation and update the PolicyEngine-US version validated against [#3190, #3192, #3195, and #3197 by Martin Holmer]

  • Require numba 0.68.0 [#3193 by Martin Holmer]

  • Refactor code to remove warnings that appeared after pandas upgrade [#3203 by Martin Holmer]

  • Update expected test results for new TMD 2.2.3 input data files [#3207 by Martin Holmer]

Bug Fixes

  • Fix four bugs reported in submission #3196 (by Xamit Kadirbekov and Daniyal Kadirbekov) [#3198 by Martin Holmer]

  • Fix calcfunctions.py typo [#3206 by Martin Holmer]

  • Fix MFS SALT deduction cap bug reported in issue #3209 [#3210 by Martin Holmer]

2026-05-18 Release 6.6.0¶

(last merged pull request is #3067)

This is an enhancement and bug-fix release.

API Changes

New Features

  • Extensive calcfunctions.py code review that improves the correspondence of Python code and local variable names with 2025 IRS tax forms (while maintaining legacy/reform tax logic) and improves calcfunctions.py documentation. [#3016 through #3067 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

  • Rename calculated variable dwks19 as dwks18 to match 2025 IRS form line number. [#3024 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

  • Rename policy parameter ALD_AlimonyReceived_hc as AlimonyReceived_frac_in_AGI. [#3026 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

  • Add policy parameter STD_Dep_earned_add and use in StdDed function logic. [#3040 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

Bug Fixes

  • Extensive calcfunctions.py code review identified and fixed several tax logic bugs, all of which had tiny effects on aggregate income tax liability; only bug fixes that had a measurable effect on 2026 current-law liability (using TMD input data) are mentioned below. [#3016 through #3067 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

  • Fix QBID bugs in TaxIncome function. Effect: tmd-26.tables: 2644.3 → 2645.3 (+0.04 percent relative change). [#3042 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

  • Fix AMT function bugs. Effect: tmd-26.tables: 2645.3 → 2644.0 (-0.05 percent relative change). [#3049 by Martin Holmer assisted by Claude Code 2.1 running Opus 4.7]

2024-06-01 Release 4.0.0¶

(last merged pull request is #2752)

This is a major release with changes that make Tax-Calculator incompatible with earlier releases.

API Changes

  • Apply a new framework for the payroll tax policy parameters: Payroll tax parameters are split into the employer side and employee side ~ FICA_mc_trt, FICA_ss_trt are replaced by FICA_mc_trt_employer, FICA_mc_trt_employee, FICA_ss_trt_employer and FICA_ss_trt_employee. [#2669 by Bodi Yang]

  • CDCC rate scale (CDCC_crt, CDCC_frt) changed from 0~1 to 0~100. [#2628 by Duncan Hobbs and #2671 by Jason DeBacker]

New Features

  • Ablility to perform payroll tax reform upon either employer side or employee side. [by Bodi Yang]

2020-08-24 Release 3.0.0¶

(last merged pull request is #2474)

This is a major release with changes that make Tax-Calculator incompatible with earlier releases.

API Changes

  • Adopt the ParamTools library for parameter processing and validation, allowing easier integration with other projects that rely on ParamTools, less code for the Tax-Calculator project to maintain, and other benefits for Tax-Calculator users. Backwards compatibiltiy was maintained except for a minor API change: The parameter values that are accessible as instance attributes (e.g. pol.II_em) are not casted down into a lower dimension. So, if the year is 2017, then pol.II_em returns [4050.0] instead of 4050.0. [#2401 by Hank Doupe]

  • CPI_offset was replaced by parameter_indexing_CPI_offset, which has slightly different behavior: When parameter_indexing_CPI_offset is specified in a reform, that value is no longer added to the existing parameter_indexing_CPI_offset as was the case with CPI_offset. Rather, the specified value becomes the offset from the baseline unchained CPI. This new behavior is consistent with what is expected from all other Tax-Calculator parameters. [#2413 by Peter Metz]

  • Replace the variable reporting the number of dependents under 5 years old (nu05) with the number under 6 years old (nu06) to support recent policy proposals. [#2443 by Peter Metz, with primary work in TaxData PR #329 by Anderson Frailey]

  • Remove the changes.md file to consolidate version reporting in this file, releases.md. [#2474 by Matt Jensen]

New Features

  • Enable Windows users to convert TAXSIM input files to the interface required by Tax-Calculator’s tc Command Line Interface by replacing validation script taxcalc.sh with taxcalc.py [#2408 by Peter Metz based on feedback from Ernie Tedeschi]

  • Add automated testing for Python 3.8 to ensure a bug-free experience for users on the latest version of Python. [#2414 by Hank Doupe]

  • Include UBI amounts, when introduced by user reforms, to variables that report total benefits. [#2418 by Jason DeBacker]

  • Improve documentation site with Jupyter Book [#2420 by Max Ghenis with auxiliary PRs by Jason DeBacker]

  • Add documentation for the Tax-Calculator API to the docs site. [#2441 by Jason DeBacker]

  • Add documentation for Tax-Calculator parameters to the docs site. [#2450 by Hank Doupe]

  • Port from SAS to Python the creation of the CPS tax unit file that is packaged with Tax-Calculator. [#2444 by Peter Metz, with primary work in TaxData PR #314 by Anderson Frailey]

  • Update the Tax-Calculator baseline for the CBO’s July 2 report, “An Update to the Economic Outlook: 2020-2030.” [#2462 by Peter Metz, with primary work in TaxData PR #332 by Jacob Chuslo]

Bug Fixes

  • Adjustments to the CPI_offset set under current law previously overwrite the scheduled expiration of TCJA tax cut for parameters that are inflation indexed. The adoption of the new parameter_indexing_CPI_offset fixes this bug. We are unware of any users encountering this issue. [#2413 by Peter Metz]
